questions.q: Why is "lakehouse" both a generic idea and a specific Fabric item name?
options: Two vendors converged on the same underlying architecture idea and largely the same file format, so the word applies at both levels
Fabric invented the term and Databricks later copied it
They are completely unrelated meanings with no real connection
Databricks no longer uses the term "lakehouse" at all
questions.explain: This is genuinely why the comparison is worth making carefully rather than assuming one specific product.

questions.q: What is identical underneath a Fabric Lakehouse table and a Databricks Delta table?
options: Both are, at the file level, Parquet data files plus a _delta_log/ folder — the same open Delta Lake specification
Nothing; they use entirely incompatible file formats
Only the file naming convention, not the actual data format
Fabric uses a proprietary format that only looks similar to Delta
questions.explain: Neither platform invented its own competing table format — both build on the same open specification.

questions.q: What compute configuration does creating a Fabric Lakehouse require, compared to Databricks?
options: None — only a capacity assignment, no VM size or runtime version like Databricks clusters require
The exact same cluster configuration steps as Databricks
Fabric requires an even more detailed compute configuration
Fabric Lakehouses cannot run any compute at all
questions.explain: This echoes Lesson 2's point about Fabric workspaces having no per-item compute decision.

questions.q: What does Fabric's Lakehouse automatically expose that doesn't have an exact Databricks & Delta Lake equivalent?
options: A SQL analytics endpoint — the same Delta data, queryable via T-SQL with zero extra configuration
A completely separate copy of the data in SQL Server format
A dedicated Spark cluster per table
Unity Catalog-style row-level security
questions.explain: This is a real convenience specific to how Fabric's Lakehouse item is structured.

questions.q: Why can a Databricks cluster potentially read a table written entirely through Fabric's UI?
options: Because both platforms are genuinely Delta underneath — an open table format rather than a proprietary one
Because Fabric automatically converts its tables to a Databricks-specific format
It's not actually possible under any circumstances
Only if the table was created using PySpark, never through the UI
questions.explain: This is the entire practical value of an open table format — a shared set of Delta files, not two incompatible islands of data.
